Read those, not all\n  of them.\n- **One check decides.** `bash .github/scripts/verify.sh` runs every check CI\n  runs, in the same order. Run it before you finish, and fix everything it\n  names. Green there is green in CI.\n- **A rule is real when something fails.** Every rule names what checks it: a\n  lint rule, the type checker, a test, the `conventions` check, or the reviewer.\n  Lint messages say how to fix; follow them.\n- **Documents over existing patterns.** Copy the code you find only where it\n  matches these documents. Where they disagree, the document wins; note the\n  difference in one line of your pull request description.\n- **These documents hold what the code cannot show.** When a reviewer flags the\n  same thing twice, it becomes a rule, with a check, in the layer it belongs to:\n  `chain/` when it holds for any project, the project's documents otherwise.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/structure.md -->\n\n# Structure\n\nWhere this project's workspaces and features are: its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## Feature folders\n\nCode is grouped by what it does for a user, not by what kind of file it is:\n\n```\napps/web/src/features/<feature>/     components, hooks, their tests\napps/api/src/features/<feature>/     routes, rules, data access, their tests\npackages/<shared>/src/<feature>.ts   what both sides share for that feature\n```\n\nA piece of work mostly stays inside one feature folder per workspace. Code used\nby two or more features moves to that workspace's `src/lib/`, and only then.\n\n**Why:** an issue is one behaviour end to end; when its code sits together, an\nagent finds all of it by path, and two issues in parallel rarely touch the same\nfiles.\n\n## Modules: small interface, real work behind it\n\nA module is a file or a feature folder with a few exports that do a lot. Prefer\none deeper module over several files that only pass calls through. Before adding\na file, ask what a caller would lose if it did not exist; if nothing, fold it in.\nSplit a module when it has two reasons to change, not when it grows.\n\n- One UI component per file, named after it (`TaskRow.tsx`).\n- Other files are kebab-case, named after what they do (`use-tasks.ts`).\n- Files stay under 300 lines. **Checked by** lint (`max-lines`).\n\n## Imports\n\n- **Named exports only**, so a search for a name finds every use. **Checked by**\n  lint (`import/no-default-export`; framework entry files are the exceptions,\n  and the lint config names them).\n- **No barrel files**: no `index.ts` that only re-exports. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Before adding\na file, ask what a caller would lose if it did not exist; if nothing, fold it in.\nSplit a module when it has two reasons to change, not when it grows.\n\n- One UI component per file, named after it (`TaskRow.tsx`).\n- Other files are kebab-case, named after what they do (`use-tasks.ts`).\n- Files stay under 300 lines. **Checked by** lint (`max-lines`).\n\n## Imports\n\n- **Named exports only**, so a search for a name finds every use. **Checked by**\n  lint (`import/no-default-export`; framework entry files are the exceptions,\n  and the lint config names them).\n- **No barrel files**: no `index.ts` that only re-exports. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Which test: [testing.md](testing.md).\n- A change that adds, renames, moves or removes a feature folder updates the\n  project's `docs/architecture.md` in the same pull request. **Checked by** the\n  `conventions` check.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/testing.md -->\n\n# Testing\n\nThe project's tools for each kind of test are named in its architecture map,\n`docs/architecture.md`.\n\n## From \"Done when\" to tests\n\nAn issue's \"Done when\" is the list of tests to write: one case, one test, named\nafter the case, so a reader can tick the issue off against the test names.\n\n| The issue says | Write | Where |\n|---|---|---|\n| A table row (`Given` → `Expect`) about a rule, a route or a function | a unit or API test per row | next to the module it tests |\n| A table row about what a component shows | a component test per row | next to the component |\n| A scenario (`Given / When / Then`) | a browser test per scenario, named after its first line | the web app's `e2e/<feature>` |\n| A row or scenario of a `Component` issue (a shared component) | a story per case, named after it, whose `play` function checks it; the story is the test | next to the component |\n\n## How tests are written\n\n- **Test through the interface**: call the module, the route or the screen the\n  way its user would. Component tests find controls by role and name, as a\n  person does. A test that has to reach past the interface means the module has\n  the wrong shape.\n- **Each test starts from nothing**: a fresh database, no data or order shared\n  with another test.\n- **No network in unit and component tests**: replace the API client at its\n  seam instead of mocking the network everywhere.\n- **Time is given, not read**: code that needs \"now\" takes it as a parameter or\n  from one clock module, so tests set it. Code used\nby two or more features moves to that workspace's `src/lib/`, and only then.\n\n**Why:** an issue is one behaviour end to end; when its code sits together, an\nagent finds all of it by path, and two issues in parallel rarely touch the same\nfiles.\n\n## Modules: small interface, real work behind it\n\nA module is a file or a feature folder with a few exports that do a lot. Prefer\none deeper module over several files that only pass calls through. Before adding\na file, ask what a caller would lose if it did not exist; if nothing, fold it in.\nSplit a module when it has two reasons to change, not when it grows.\n\n- One UI component per file, named after it (`TaskRow.tsx`).\n- Other files are kebab-case, named after what they do (`use-tasks.ts`).\n- Files stay under 300 lines. **Checked by** lint (`max-lines`).\n\n## Imports\n\n- **Named exports only**, so a search for a name finds every use. **Checked by**\n  lint (`import/no-default-export`; framework entry files are the exceptions,\n  and the lint config names them).\n- **No barrel files**: no `index.ts` that only re-exports. Import from the file\n  that defines the thing. **Checked by** lint. Barrels are where parallel changes\n  collide, and they hide where code lives.\n- **Between workspaces, by package name**, never by a relative path into another\n  workspace. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-relative-packages`).\n- **No import cycles.** **Checked by** lint (`import/no-cycle`).\n- **Only declared dependencies**: import a package only if the importing\n  workspace declares it. **Checked by** lint (`import/no-extraneous-dependencies`).\n\nDependencies, configuration and CI are people's work: package manifests,\nlockfiles and `.github/` cannot be changed by an agent (gh-aw protected files).\nIf a change needs a new dependency, say so in the pull request instead.\n\n## Code comes with tests, the map comes with features\n\n- A change to source files changes or adds a test that proves it. **Checked by**\n  the `conventions` check. Component tests find controls by role and name, as a\n  person does. A test that has to reach past the interface means the module has\n  the wrong shape.\n- **Each test starts from nothing**: a fresh database, no data or order shared\n  with another test.\n- **No network in unit and component tests**: replace the API client at its\n  seam instead of mocking the network everywhere.\n- **Time is given, not read**: code that needs \"now\" takes it as a parameter or\n  from one clock module, so tests set it. Date logic is tested at fixed times,\n  including just before and after midnight.\n- **Never weaken or delete a test to make a check pass.** If a test is wrong, say\n  why in the pull request.\n\n---\n\n<!-- docs/architecture.md -->\n\n# Tempo architecture\n\nTempo is a task app: people sign in and manage their own tasks, by list and by\nproject. Data comes through one client\n\nAll calls to the API go through `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`, which parses\nevery response with its schema from `@tempo/shared`. Components and hooks never\ncall `fetch` themselves. **Checked by** lint (`no-restricted-globals: fetch`\noutside the client).\n\n**Why:** one seam to replace in tests, one place where the contract is enforced,\nand a response that does not match its schema fails loudly instead of rendering\nwrong.\n\n## Components\n\n- Screens are built from the shared components (`components.md`): reuse one,\n  never rebuild it inside a feature. A part the design repeats that has no\n  shared component yet is a `Component` issue first.\n- A feature's screen state lives in a hook next to it (`use-tasks.ts`); the\n  component renders what the hook returns. Keep components free of API and\n  date logic, so the logic is tested without rendering.\n- Every screen state the design shows (loading, empty, error, disabled) is a\n  state the component can be put in, and a test puts it there.\n- Routing uses React Router: every screen is one entry in\n  `apps/web/src/routes.tsx`, and its component lives in its feature folder.\n\n## Forms\n\nValidate with the same schema the API uses (`@tempo/shared`), so the form and\nthe API refuse the same things with the same messages. Show errors where the\ndesign shows them, on the field, in the design's words.\n\n## Styling\n\n- Tailwind v4, configured in CSS: the theme is the `@theme` block in\n  `apps/web/src/index.css`. There is no `tailwind.config` file.\n- Tailwind classes only, with the design's colours and font through the theme.\n  The design's variables map to tokens: `$bg` → `bg-bg`, `$surface` →\n  `bg-surface`, `$border` → `border-border`, `$text` → `text-text`, `$muted` →\n  `text-muted`, `$faint` → `text-faint`, `$accent` → `bg-accent` /\n  `text-accent`, `$accent-soft` → `bg-accent-soft`, `$danger` → `text-danger`,\n  `$font` → Inter. Keyboard shortcuts the design shows (`⌘ N`) work. **Checked by**\nlint (`jsx-a11y-x`), and by tests that find controls by role and name.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/chain/design.md -->\n\n# Building from the design\n\n## How a pen file is built\n\nA `.pen` file is JSON: a tree of elements, each with a stable `id` (it never\nchanges when the element is edited or moved) and a `name` that says what it is.\n\n- **Top-level children are frames and components.** A frame is a screen or a\n  state of one (\"Auth — Sign In Error\"); a component (`\"reusable\": true`) is a\n  shared part (\"Form Field / Text\", \"Menu Item\").\n- **A component is used through a `ref`:** `{\"type\": \"ref\", \"ref\": \"<component\n  id>\"}` stands where the component appears, with its own `id` and any\n  overrides (`descendants`, keyed by id path). Two screens using the Text field\n  hold two refs with different ids, both pointing at one component. Claim the\n  component to build it, and the screen to build the screen.\n- **Variables are tokens:** `\"variables\"` maps a name to a value; elements refer\n  to them as `$name`. Each has a theme token in `apps/web/src/index.css`, and a\n  test keeps the two equal, so a token change lands with its theme change.\n- **Scripts** (`.github/scripts/`): `design-part.sh <pen> <id>` prints one part\n  with every component resolved in place; `design-diff.sh <old> <new>` lists\n  what changed, element by element; `design-impact.sh` maps those changes to\n  the issues whose claims they touch, through the components each part uses;\n  `design-claims.sh <pen>` lists every frame with the issues claiming it.\n\nAn issue names the design parts it builds under \"## Design\", as\n`<path>.pen#<id>`. Before you start, those parts are extracted for you:\n\n- `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/design/index.md` lists them;\n- `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/design/<id>.json` holds each part exactly: sizes, spacing,\n  colours, text and the elements inside it, each with a `name` that says what it\n  is. An element with `\"component\": {\"id\", \"name\"}` is a use of a shared\n  component, shown with this use's own text and settings;\n- `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/design/variables.json` holds the values parts refer to as\n  `$name` (for example `$accent`).\n\nRead them with `jq`. They are the specification; the images in the issue show the\nsame parts, for people.\n\n## Turning the design into code\n\n- **Variables are theme tokens.** Each design variable has a token in the\n  project's theme (the mapping is in the project's web document). Use the token,\n  never the value.\n- **Sizes and spacing** come from the part's JSON: `gap`, `padding`, `width`,\n  `height`, `cornerRadius`. Use the theme's step that matches the value; a value\n  with no step is a reason to check the design again, not to invent one.\n- **Text** is copied exactly, punctuation included.\n- **A component is built once.** Where the part uses a component, use the\n  project's existing component for it; what differs between uses (text, colour,\n  a hidden part) becomes that component's props or variants, not a copy.\n- **Build only what the issue claims.** A part the issue lists under \"Out of\n  scope\" is hidden, not built half-way, even when it appears in the design.\n\nDesign files are people's: an agent never edits them.\n\n---\n\n<!-- .github/conventions/components.md -->\n\n# Shared components\n\nA screen is built from shared components. A component is finished, in every\nstate the design gives it, before a screen uses it; a screen never builds its\nown copy of one.\n\n## Where they live\n\n- One folder per component: `apps/web/src/components/<Name>/`, holding\n  `<Name>.tsx` and `<Name>.stories.tsx`. Import it by that file's path; there\n  are no `index.ts` re-exports (lint, `no-barrel-files`).\n- Before building anything, look in the web app's `src/components/` for what\n  exists and reuse it. A component that needs a new variant gets it in its own\n  folder, not a copy elsewhere.\n- The class-merging helper `cn` is in the web app's `src/lib/utils.ts`.\n\n## How they are written\n\nThe shadcn/ui way, which is also how agents know it best:\n\n- **Behaviour from Radix** (the `radix-ui` package) wherever the design has an\n  interactive pattern it covers: menus, dialogs, checkboxes, popovers. Keyboard\n  and screen-reader behaviour then come built in. A plain element needs none.\n- **Variants with `cva`** (`class-variance-authority`); classes combined with\n  `cn`, so a caller's `className` wins over the defaults.\n- **Composition over configuration**: `children`, and `asChild` (Radix `Slot`)\n  to render as another element. Add a prop only for a real variant the design\n  shows.\n- **Native props pass through**: a `Button` takes everything a `button` does,\n  `ref` included (a plain prop in React 19).\n- **Design tokens only** (`web.md`, \"Styling\"); sizes from the claimed parts'\n  JSON. Icons from `lucide-react`.\n- **No API calls, dates or app state.** A component renders what it is given.\n\n## Stories are its tests\n\nEach state the design shows is one story. Its `args` put the component in that\nstate; its `play` function acts (clicks, types, keys) and asserts, with\n`expect` and `within` from `storybook/test`. A \"Done when\" case is a story named\nafter it (`.github/conventions/chain/testing.md`).\n\n- **Assert what a person perceives**: the role and accessible name, the text,\n  the state (checked, disabled, expanded, focused). Never class names\n  (`toHaveClass('bg-accent')`): they repeat the implementation, so every styling\n  change breaks them without anything being wrong (implement run 36674016191\n  spent 20 edits on that).
